Maria (Support): FYI escalation from Acme - their integration using JSON-mode keeps returning 400 / Invalid JSON when payload includes nested arrays/objects. Customer says this started after last night's runtime rollout. P0. Sample below, repro steps included.

Maria (Support): Request (redacted headers) and payload they sent: 
```curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \u0024' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","response_format":"json","input":{"user_id":"acct_123","items":[{"id":"i1","attributes":[{"value":"x"}]},{"attributes":[{"name":"a","value":"y"}],"tmp":true}]}}'
```

Maria (Support): Response they received: 
```json
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"Invalid JSON", "message":"could not parse structured output"}
```

AJ (Backend): Can you paste the full server-side parse log for the X-Request-ID? Also: are they using streaming/chunked responses? Is `response_format: "json"` or `structured: true`?

Maria (Support): X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d. They are not streaming. Server log excerpt: 
```
json_parser.cpp:142 parse error at offset 185, path /items/1/attributes: missing required key 'name'
validator.cpp:78 schema mismatch: expected object with keys [name,value] but got partial object
```

Maria (Support): Note: rollout tag on runtime is `runtime-v2.3.0` deployed 2025-11-06 02:13 UTC. Customer says previously they got a best-effort output (we would fill nulls), now it's a hard 400.

Olivia (QA): Repro steps I ran locally (same as customer) - I can reproduce 400. Interesting: if I add `id` to every attribute object or include `name` on the partial object it succeeds. If I reorder the items array so the problematic element is first sometimes it passes. Looks like validator is indexing items by position and expecting positional schema mapping.

Olivia (QA): Repro curl I used: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @payload.json
# payload.json same as customer
```

Kevin (SRE): Two quick Qs: 1) any rate-limit or auth spikes when they retried? 2) can we route just this customer's traffic to the previous runtime version as a mitigation? We can do a canary reroute in the next 10-15m.

Maria (Support): They hit a 401 when they swapped API keys in one retry (they were testing multiple env keys). Main issue is the 400 on valid-ish JSON. Customer prefers we not change client.

AJ (Backend): Root cause hypothesis: validator in v2.3 switched to a strict positional-schema mode to optimize allocation of KV caches for streaming. That change treats arrays as positional typed-rows and enforces exact keys per position. It fails when clients send partial objects or add extra keys.

AJ (Backend): Quick fixes: 
- Emergency: route Acme to `runtime-v2.2.8` (last known good). Kevin can do.
- Short term: add a permissive flag on the validator `allow_unknown_keys=true` and `tolerate_missing_fields=true` for legacy compatibility; return warnings instead of hard 400.
- Long term: change validator to validate by object shape, not by position, and include JSON Pointer in error messages (e.g. `/items/1/attributes/0/name missing`).

Kevin (SRE): I can route them to v2.2.8 now. Doing canary: routing req_0a1b2c3d -> v2.2.8 for their account id acct_123. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: Starting canary reroute for acct_123 -> runtime-v2.2.8 (10% traffic)

Olivia (QA): Test matrix I'll run after reroute: payload variants with missing keys, extra keys, reordered arrays, nested empty arrays. Need to add unit tests for positional vs shape-based validation. I'll create a test PR.

AJ (Backend): I'll open a hotfix PR to add permissive flags and improve error payloads. Include path pointer and an example of the expected shape in the error. Also ensure streaming/kv-cache optimization isn't the default breaking client behavior.

Rachel (CS): Can someone draft a short customer-facing note/workaround I can send to Acme: suggest they include explicit `name` fields or remove extra keys; we'll route them and push a fix. Keep message non-technical.

Maria (Support): Draft for customer: "Thanks — we see this is caused by a recent runtime change to structured parsing. As a workaround please ensure nested objects include required fields (e.g., `name`). We've routed your traffic to a compatible runtime and are deploying a fix; ETA ~ 4 hours." Thoughts?

AJ (Backend): fine. Add: "We will update API error responses to include the exact JSON path causing the failure."

Kevin (SRE): Canary shows Acme traffic to v2.2.8 succeeded for 50 recent requests. No other customers flagged. I'll escalate rollback if more accounts report.

Olivia (QA): Assigned owners: AJ -> patch PR, Kevin -> routing/monitoring, Olivia -> tests, Maria -> customer comms. ETA hotfix: 3-6h.

Maria (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and send the customer note. Marking thread P0.
